title: Positive real spectrum of the comparison of ample polarizations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $L,M$ be ample invertible modules on $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Use the dual variety and line-module homomorphisms of [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field]. Put $E=\operatorname{End}_k(A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, with composition as multiplication, using [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Set
$$\lambda=\phi_L,\qquad u=\lambda^{-1}\phi_M\in E,\qquad v^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}v^\vee\lambda.$$
Then $u^\dagger=u$. Let $C=\mathbf Q[u]\subseteq E$ be the image of the polynomial evaluation map $\mathbf Q[T]\to E$, $T\mapsto u$. This is a finite-dimensional commutative unital $\mathbf Q$-algebra. For some integer $d\geq0$ there is an isomorphism of unital $\mathbf R$-algebras
$$\rho:C\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R^d$$
such that every coordinate of $\rho(u\otimes1)$ is strictly positive. Here $\mathbf R^d$ has coordinatewise addition and multiplication; a $\mathbf Q$-algebra is a ring with a unital map from $\mathbf Q$, and finite-dimensional means that its underlying $\mathbf Q$-vector space has a finite basis. The zero algebra and $d=0$ are allowed (in particular when $\dim A=0$), with the positivity condition then vacuous. No symmetry of $L$ or $M$, and no characteristic or algebraic-closedness hypothesis on $k$, is required.

source.place: Agent auxiliary for the abelian endomorphism-span input: consequence of I Proposition 14.2 and Theorem 14.3, pp.61–62, Theorem 11.1, p.54, and Proposition 10.20 / Corollary 10.24, pp.50–53. The positive-spectrum deduction, including arbitrary-field descent, is written in the report; this is not a separately numbered theorem in Milne.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], $A_K$ is abelian of the same dimension; [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change], with base $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $L_K,M_K$ ample. The normalized Poincare universal property of [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum] restricts to $K$-schemes: $A_K\times_K T=A\times_k T$, so the base-changed datum represents the required families. Uniqueness identifies $(A^\vee)_K$ with $(A_K)^\vee$. The translated-difference and dual-pullback families also base change, hence their classifying maps, inverses in rational Hom, and dagger do so. The map $j:E\to\operatorname{End}^0_K(A_K)$ is injective: after multiplying a putative kernel element by a positive integer, its geometric Tate action is zero, so [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-action-saturation] makes the integral endomorphism zero. We use geometry over $K$ below, but keep $C=\mathbf Q[u]$ over the original field.

source.place: §§8–10: normalized Poincare universal property, field extension and faithful geometric Tate action; Stacks Tag 0893 for ample base change

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free], a finite integral basis of $\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ becomes a rational basis of $E$. Thus $E$ and its subspace $C$ are finite-dimensional. The image of polynomial evaluation is a commutative unital subalgebra, since powers of one element commute. By [lem-pc-ample-affine-loci-criterion], applied to the proper $K$-scheme $A_K$, the module $L_K$, ample in the affine-nonvanishing-locus sense by step 1, is ample in the sense required by [lem-sfb-rosati-trace-positive]. Restrict the positive symmetric form of [lem-sfb-rosati-trace-positive] along $j$, obtaining $B(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_K}(j(x)^\dagger j(y))$ on $E$; injectivity makes it positive definite. If $g=\dim A=0$, [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-action-saturation] gives Tate rank zero and injectivity, whence $E=C=0$; take $d=0$. Henceforth $g>0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.15 p.49 and Theorem 14.3 p.62; zero-dimensional case by Tate faithfulness

proof.text: Over $K$ write $e_L(x,y)=e(x,V_\ell(\lambda)y)$ and $e_M(x,y)=e(x,V_\ell(\phi_M)y)$ for a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}K$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-weil-pairing] both are alternating; perfection and the rational inverse to $\lambda$ make $e_L$ nondegenerate. Since $\lambda u=\phi_M$, $e_L(x,uy)=e_M(x,y)$. Consequently $e_L(ux,y)=-e_L(y,ux)=-e_M(y,x)=e_M(x,y)=e_L(x,uy)$. Functoriality of the Weil pairing and the formula for dagger in [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field] give $e_L(ux,y)=e_L(x,u^\dagger y)$. Nondegeneracy identifies the two Tate operators; after clearing denominators, [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-action-saturation] identifies the rational endomorphisms. Injection of $j$ then gives $u^\dagger=u$ over $k$.

source.place: Proposition 14.2 pp.61–62: its symmetry direction, written via the alternating pairings of §13

proof.text: Dagger fixes every polynomial in $u$, because it fixes rational scalars and $u$ and reverses products. Hence on $C$, $B(c,d)=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_K}(j(cd))$, and multiplication by $u$ is symmetric: $B(uc,d)=B(c,ud)$. By [lem-sfb-rational-symmetric-form-orthogonal-basis], choose an orthogonal rational basis of $C$. Its nonzero basis vectors have strictly positive rational squared lengths. Extending scalars to $\mathbf R$ gives the positive form $\sum_i B(e_i,e_i)x_i^2$, hence an inner product on $C_{\mathbf R}=C\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf R$. Multiplication by $u\otimes1$ remains symmetric. Apply [lem-sfb-real-symmetric-orthonormal-eigenbasis] to obtain an eigenbasis with real eigenvalues.

source.place: Theorem 14.3 p.62, finite-dimensional linear-algebra deduction; pinned Mathlib spectral theorem

proof.text: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ be the distinct eigenvalues just obtained. Every element of $C_{\mathbf R}$ is a real polynomial in $u\otimes1$: expand a tensor in rational powers of $u$ and collect its real coefficients. For such a polynomial define $\rho(p(u\otimes1))=(p(a_i))_i$. This is well defined and injective: on each eigenvector multiplication by $p(u\otimes1)$ is $p(a_i)$, and the regular representation is faithful, since multiplication by $c$ sends $1$ to $c$. It is onto: the Lagrange polynomials $\prod_{j\ne i}(T-a_j)/(a_i-a_j)$ map to the coordinate unit vectors. Therefore $\rho$ is a unital real-algebra isomorphism, and $\rho(u\otimes1)=(a_i)_i$.

source.place: Agent algebra calculation from the preceding eigenbasis: polynomial evaluation and Lagrange interpolation

proof.text: We check the isogeny hypothesis needed for the degree calculation. Over $K$, [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] gives $\dim A_K^\vee=g$. Clear denominators in the inverse from [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field]: for some $n>0$ there is an integral $h:A_K^\vee\to A_K$ with $\lambda h=[n]$. This equality holds integrally because Hom is torsion-free by [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free]. The map $[n]$ is surjective by [lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny], so $\lambda$ is surjective. Since source and target have the same dimension, [lem-sfb-equal-dimension-isogeny-criterion] makes $\lambda$ an isogeny.

source.place: §§7–11: rational inverse and the isogeny criterion; Proposition 8.1 and §8 dual dimension

proof.text:
All intersections in this step are on $A_K$. Put $c_i=(L_K^iM_K^{g-i}\cdot A_K)$, $b=(L_K^g\cdot A_K)/g!$, and $Q(T)=\sum_{i=0}^g\binom gi c_iT^i/g!$. For each integer $n\geq0$, [lem-sfb-top-intersection-multilinear] gives $Q(n)=((L_K^{\otimes n}\otimes M_K)^g\cdot A_K)/g!$. By [lem-sfb-polarization-calculus-over-field], the associated homomorphism is $n\lambda+\phi_M$. Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-relative-tate-determinant] with this homomorphism and the inverse of $\lambda$. The formula [lem-sfb-abelian-line-bundle-degree-square], applied to this line and to $L_K$, gives
$$\det(n\,1+V_\ell(u))=Q(n)^2/b^2.$$
By [lem-sfb-ample-mixed-intersection-positive], $b>0$. Let $P=P_{-j(u)}\in\mathbf Q[T]$ from [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-charpoly]; it maps to $\det(T\,1+V_\ell(u))$. Thus $P(n)=Q(n)^2/b^2$ in $\mathbf Q$, by injectivity of $\mathbf Q\to\mathbf Q_\ell$. The two polynomials agree at infinitely many integers, so $P(T)=Q(T)^2/b^2$.

source.place: Proposition 10.20 pp.50–52 and Theorem 11.1 p.54; Stacks Tags 0BER and 0BEV for expansion and positivity

proof.text: For every $i$, [lem-sfb-ample-mixed-intersection-positive] gives $c_i>0$. Hence $Q(t)>0$ for every real $t\geq0$: its terms are nonnegative and its constant term $c_0/g!$ is positive. The polynomial identity of the preceding step implies $P(t)>0$ there. On the other hand, [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module], applied to $-V_\ell(u)$ and the characteristic polynomial supplied by [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-charpoly], gives $P(-j(u))=0$: first the Tate operator vanishes, then [lem-sfb-abelian-tate-action-saturation] removes it after clearing denominators. Injection of $j$ gives $P(-u)=0$ in $C$. Applying $\rho$ yields $P(-a_i)=0$ for every coordinate. Positivity of $P$ on $[0,\infty)$ forces $-a_i<0$, so $a_i>0$. This proves the required positivity with no symmetry assumption on either line and over the original arbitrary field.
